chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Majiluwayh narrated to me, saying: Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar narrated to me from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Ahmad ibn Hilal from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr from Aban from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:

Indeed, when the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) returned from Arafat and proceeded to Mina, he entered the mosque, and the people gathered around him asking him about the Night of Qadr. He stood as a preacher and said, after praising Allah: 'As for what follows, which of you asked me about the Night of Qadr? I did not conceal it from you because I did not know about it.'

Know, O people, that whoever witnesses the month of Ramadan while being healthy and sound, fasts its days, spends a portion of its nights in prayer, maintains his prayers, attends the Friday prayers, and sets out for the Eid prayer, has indeed attained the Night of Qadr and has earned the reward of the Lord.
He said, and Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: 'By Allah, he has earned rewards that are not like the rewards of people.'
ai.seo_question: How does one attain the Night of Qadr according to this hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from Shaykh al-Saduq, the Prophet Muhammad (peace be upon him) reveals that the Night of Qadr is not a fixed date known only to him, but a spiritual station attained through the consistent practice of fasting, night prayer, and communal loyalty during Ramadan. Imam Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) emphasizes that the reward for this specific devotion transcends ordinary acts of worship, highlighting the Shia emphasis on the integration of ritual piety with social and communal fidelity (hijra to the congregation) as the key to unlocking divine grace.

en.sayed-athar-husain-rizvi-&-sayed-maqs: 3. It was narrated to me by Muhammad b. Ali b. Majluwayh who said it was narrated to me by Muhammad b. Yahya al-’Attar from Muhammad b. Ahmad b. Ahmad b. Hilal from Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Abi Nasr from Aban from Abi Ja’far (a.s.) who said:

"When the Prophet (sw) returned from 'Arafat and proceeded to Mina, he entered the mosque, and people gathered around him asking about the Night of Qadr. He stood as a preacher and said, after praising Allah, 'Now then, which of you asked me about the Night of Qadr? I did not withhold it from you because I did not know about it.

Know, O people, that whoever witnesses the month of Ramadan while being healthy and sound, fasts during its days, spends a portion of its nights in prayer, maintains his prayers, attends the Friday prayers, and sets out for the Eid prayer, has indeed attained the Night of Qadr and has earned the reward of the Lord.’
Then Abu Abdullah (as) said: 'By Allah, he has earned rewards that are unlike the rewards given by people.'"
